note: Find the cell or text box and retype one label. Reasoning: a single targeted keystroke edit plus a visual re-check is about a minute. No published per-edit time exists for this class.

Trace one figure back to the filing line, correct it and confirm the dependants still tie. Reasoning: opening the 10-K page and re-checking 2-3 dependants is about 5 minutes; the WSP 3-statement task (1-3 hrs for roughly 150 sourced inputs) implies a few minutes per traced input at most.

Locate a broken or inconsistent formula, repair it, copy it across the row and re-run the checks. Reasoning: the audit trail walk is the slow part; the IB review checklist in docs/buyer-research.md section 1a (one row, one formula; checks roll up) implies a row-by-row check.

Repoint a broken cross-sheet or cross-slide reference and verify the target. Reasoning: shorter than a formula fix because the target is known, longer than a label because dependants must be re-checked.
Change a chart type, series or axis and re-fit labels and the source line. Reasoning: the edit is quick but chart formatting (labels, units, scale) takes several tries.

Re-order or re-flow a slide or section: move shapes, re-write the action title, re-align and re-validate. Reasoning: BankerToolBench-style pitchbook rework is the slowest per-edit class short of a missing section; 20 minutes is a lower-end guess.

Write or build a section the draft omitted (for example a risks page or a valuation paragraph) with sources. Reasoning: a short paragraph or a one-slide build with sourcing; a full missing analysis would be much longer and is not covered by this row.
Attach a filing page, quote or XBRL concept to a figure that has none, and confirm the as-of date. Reasoning: find the page, copy the locator, check the figure matches the quote.
Fix alignment, number format, font size or colour convention on one item. Reasoning: format-painter or style fix on one element; batches are cheaper per item, so this is a per-item upper estimate.
